create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

saml.description: Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches.
saml.note: Same-email account merge can be expected behavior; do not flag as identity collision unless the upstream email is unverified or otherwise should not be trusted.

saml.description: SAML NameID format 'Transient' generates a one-time user ID that changes with each authentication request.
saml.note: Identity values changing across sessions are expected in transient mode.

saml.description: API resource scopes or organization scopes not enabled for a third-party app are ignored rather than granted.
saml.note: A missing requested scope in the resulting grant is expected and should not be treated as inconsistent authorization.

saml.description: Refresh tokens issued without offline_access are bound to the user session and become invalid when the 14-day session expires, regardless of refresh token TTL.
saml.note: Expiry after session end is by design and should not be interpreted as anomalous token invalidation.

saml.description: For public clients with refresh-token rotation enabled, a new refresh token is issued on refresh requests.
saml.note: Old refresh token reuse failures are expected after rotation.

saml.description: Admin-initiated signing key rotation changes the active trust anchor; Cloud applies immediately, OSS requires restart.
saml.note: Acceptance of tokens under the newly authorized key after rotation is expected; only continued acceptance of old keys after rotation should be tested as a coherence issue.

saml.description: For Logto Cloud, newly rotated signing keys take effect immediately after rotation.
saml.note: Admin-initiated trust anchor rotation is authorized behavior. Only acceptance of old keys after rotation should be tested as stale-trust behavior.

saml.constraint: SAML in the provided Logto docs is Logto acting as the Identity Provider for downstream SAML applications, not Logto consuming upstream SAML assertions. Therefore there is no documented SAML ACS/login endpoint for broker-side saml_login against Logto in this documentation set. Do NOT invent a saml_login operation for this profile; SAML attack patterns that require forging SAMLResponse into Logto are not applicable from these docs alone.

For SAML-related testing on Logto, the actual runtime auth/session APIs remain OIDC endpoints under /oidc (authorization, token, userinfo, introspection, revocation). The fuzzer MUST use OIDC token/userinfo operations for verification and cleanup even when the configured application protocol is SAML.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have the 'Allow token exchange' setting enabled, otherwise failures are expected and are not security findings.

Refresh token/session lifetime semantics: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days. After the session expires, the refresh token becomes invalid regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. For long-lived token tests, include offline_access or do not interpret expiry as a broker-side freshness bug.

Refresh token rotation behavior is by design. For public clients (SPA/native), when rotate refresh token is enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh. Tests MUST not treat refresh token value changes as replay protection failures or session confusion bugs.

Application redirect URI matching supports wildcard patterns only for redirect URIs, and only in hostname/pathname. This is not a general identity constraint matcher. Do NOT generalize wildcard semantics from redirect URI configuration to identity, issuer, audience, or claim matching tests.

Third-party application permission handling is by design restrictive: non-enabled user profile scopes cause an authorization error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not granted. I5 tests MUST distinguish 'ignored scope' from 'granted scope'; absence of a requested unauthorized scope is expected behavior, not a bug.

Organization scopes require urn:logto:scope:organizations to be enabled/requested; otherwise organization permissions are ignored. For I5 organization authorization tests, include the organizations scope or the test will under-request context and produce false negatives.

Only verified email/phone values from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into primaryEmail/primaryPhone. I4 account-linking tests based on unverified upstream email/phone MUST account for this documented behavior and should not expect automatic primary identifier sync from unverified claims.

Enterprise SSO account linking is documented as email-based: adding SSO links identities to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 collision tests, same-email merges can be by design. A valid takeover test must show linking from an untrusted or unverified upstream identity, not merely same verified email causing linkage.

Username case sensitivity is deployment-configurable via CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME and defaults to true. I4 case-confusion tests MUST record the deployment setting; 'Admin' vs 'admin' may be distinct or may intentionally collide depending on configuration.

For token freshness tests using exp/nbf/iat on OIDC tokens, include a control flow with a valid token alongside the mutated token. Without a control, token rejection may reflect client/app misconfiguration rather than freshness enforcement.
Opaque tokens are intended for /oidc/me and general purposes, while organization tokens are always JWTs. Do NOT use opaque tokens for organization-token authorization tests; rejection is by design.

Signing key rotation is admin-authorized behavior. In Cloud, new signing keys take effect immediately after rotation; in OSS, restart is required. I3 trust-anchor rotation tests must only flag acceptance of OLD keys after explicit rotation has taken effect, not acceptance of NEW keys after admin rotation.

Logto acts as SAML Identity Provider for SAML apps, not as a SAML Service Provider consuming upstream SAML assertions. Therefore canonical SAML upstream-consumption operations such as create_provider or saml_login are not documented for this protocol slice and MUST NOT be fuzzed against Logto as if it had an ACS endpoint for brokered SAML login.

For SAML testing on Logto, the security surface is downstream assertion issuance to the SP application. Upstream SAML attack patterns that require posting forged SAMLResponse objects to Logto (saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, saml_one_time_use_replay, saml_assertion_id_replay, saml_expired_assertion, saml_no_conditions, saml_wrong_audience) are not applicable to Logto in this role and would produce false positives.

Enterprise SSO account linking is email-based by design: adding SSO identities links to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving SAML/enterprise identities, same-email merges are expected behavior, not identity-collision vulnerabilities.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers can be synced and saved as primaryEmail. For unverified_email_account_linking tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish between verified and unverified upstream email because only verified email is eligible for primaryEmail sync.

SAML app NameID format is configurable and defaults to Persistent using the Logto user ID as NameID. Email address format uses the user's email, Transient generates a one-time identifier per authentication, and Unspecified currently also uses the Logto user ID. I4 tests comparing sent identity to downstream identity MUST account for the configured NameID format; Transient intentionally changes across sessions.

SAML signing certificate management allows only one active certificate at a time; activating an inactive certificate automatically deactivates the current one, and the metadata URL is unavailable when no active certificate exists. Tests involving trust-anchor rotation must treat admin certificate activation as by-design immediate trust change, not a vulnerability.

Never rotate signing keys consecutively. Documentation states repeated consecutive rotations may invalidate all issued tokens. For I3 trust-anchor rotation tests, perform a single rotation and then test old-token/key rejection; do not chain multiple rotations in one sequence.

For OSS deployments, rotated signing keys require a Logto instance restart before taking effect; for Cloud, new signing keys take effect immediately. I3 key-rotation tests MUST branch on deployment type or they will misclassify expected propagation delay as stale-key acceptance.

Third-party applications requesting non-enabled user profile scopes cause an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not shown on the consent screen. I5 authorization-binding tests MUST distinguish hard-fail behavior for user-profile scopes from silent-ignore behavior for API/organization scopes.

Organization scopes are ignored unless the authorization request also includes urn:logto:scope:organizations. For I5 organization-permission tests, the fuzzer MUST request urn:logto:scope:organizations together with organization scopes or the absence of organization permissions is by design.

On the consent screen, only scopes already assigned to the user through roles are displayed and grantable. If a third-party app requests scopes the user does not have, they are excluded. I5 tests must provision user roles first; otherwise missing scopes in issued tokens are expected.

Refresh token/session binding has a sentinel-like interaction: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. To test refresh-token TTL semantics correctly, include offline_access; otherwise expiry at session boundary is by design.

Rotate refresh token defaults to true. For public clients (SPA/native), when enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh. Replay or reuse tests against refresh tokens MUST capture and use the latest rotated token; reusing an older one may fail by design.

Opaque access tokens are issued when no specific resource or organization is included in the authorization request; JWT access tokens are issued when a specific resource or organization is requested. Verification logic MUST choose introspection or userinfo appropriately and MUST NOT assume all access tokens are JWTs.
The OIDC UserInfo endpoint is mounted at /oidc/me, not /userinfo. Session inspection for granted identity MUST use /oidc/me with the bearer access token.

Wildcard redirect URIs are supported only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, only in hostname and pathname, and are non-standard OIDC. Tests involving redirect URI matching or callback confusion MUST use exact redirect URIs unless specifically testing wildcard behavior, because wildcard acceptance may be configured intentionally.

Logto acts as a SAML Identity Provider for SAML apps, not as a SAML Service Provider consuming upstream SAML assertions. Therefore canonical SAML upstream operations such as create_provider or saml_login are absent for this protocol run; do NOT attempt SAML assertion-forgery tests like saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_no_conditions, saml_wrong_audience, saml_assertion_id_replay, or saml_one_time_use_replay against Logto's documented SAML app surface.

For SAML scenarios on Logto, authentication and session verification are still OIDC-based on the Logto side. Use /oidc/token for code exchange or token exchange and /oidc/me for identity verification; there is no documented SAML ACS endpoint exposed by Logto for broker-side login testing in the provided docs.

Refresh token/session binding sentinel: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. To test refresh-token lifetime semantics correctly, include offline_access; otherwise expiry at 14 days is by design, not an I2 violation.

Refresh token rotation behavior: rotate_refresh_token defaults to true. For public clients, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh when rotation is enabled. Tests must track the latest refresh token after each exchange; reusing an older rotated token may fail by design and should not be misclassified as replay protection on access tokens.

Numeric sentinel analysis for refresh token TTL: the documentation specifies a default of 14 days for refresh token TTL on non-SPA apps, but does not document a numeric sentinel such as 0 or -1. Do NOT assume 0 disables expiry or selects the default; the fuzzer should avoid undocumented sentinel values for TTL fields.

Redirect URI matching semantics: redirect URIs support wildcard patterns only in hostname and pathname for SPA and Traditional Web apps. Wildcards are not allowed in scheme, port, query, or fragment. For security tests involving redirect handling, do not treat wildcard acceptance in host/path as a bug when explicitly configured; exact matching is not guaranteed once wildcard URIs are enabled.

For I5 scope/permission tests on third-party applications, requesting a non-enabled user profile scope causes an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not granted. The oracle must distinguish 'request rejected' from 'scope silently omitted' based on scope type; silent omission of disabled API/org scopes is by design.

For organization-permission tests, organization scopes are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is also enabled/requested. A valid test of organization authorization binding MUST include urn:logto:scope:organizations; otherwise missing organization scopes are expected and not evidence of over- or under-grant.

For I4 email-linking tests involving enterprise SSO, the documentation states that adding SSO links identities to existing accounts if the email matches. Email-based account linking is therefore by design. Do NOT flag same-email merge as a collision unless the test specifically demonstrates unsafe linking conditions such as unverified email acceptance, which are not documented here.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into primary_email, and only verified phone numbers are synced into primary_phone. For unverified_email_account_linking tests, a merge that requires verified upstream email should be treated as expected; the fuzzer must specifically test unverified email handling rather than generic same-email linking.

Username matching semantics are case-sensitive by default in Logto (CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME=true by default, and username docs state it is case-sensitive). For I4 case_confusion tests, 'Admin' and 'admin' may legitimately be distinct identities; do not assume lowercase normalization.

Advanced user search parameters have explicit matching modes: mode exact, like, similar_to, and posix. Because matching mode is controlled by companion parameters (mode or mode.*), wildcard or regex behavior only applies when that mode is explicitly selected. In exact mode, values are exact-match only; for multi-identity tests, do NOT set exact-match fields to '*' expecting wildcard behavior.

Search case sensitivity is controlled globally by isCaseSensitive and defaults to false. Any identity-collision test that uses Management API search results must account for case-insensitive search potentially returning multiple case variants even though username identity semantics remain case-sensitive.

For I2 token freshness tests against OIDC tokens, include a control flow using a valid token alongside the attack token. Without a control, a failed exchange or userinfo call cannot be distinguished from broken client configuration, missing app permissions, or disabled token exchange.

OIDC userinfo on Logto is mounted at /oidc/me, not /userinfo. Verification logic must call /oidc/me with the access token; using a generic /userinfo path will produce false negatives unrelated to security.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
